status: diagnostic hypotheses; no implementation experiment or measured gain
scope: Preserve current-tick contact/stress, at most one correction, equilibrium, ordinary APIs and sleep. Screen light7 then full52 and continuous warm idle/heavy. Savings below are non-additive hypotheses, not counter-derived predictions.

experiments.hypothesis: Remove duplicate fragment compatibility/lifecycle preparation at existing producer boundaries
experiments.evidence: First-impact and late-debris timelines have substantially more launches, copies and host decisions than idle. Prior dataflow audit identifies compatibility allocation/registration on the critical path; its older warm timings require revalidation.
experiments.mechanism: Identify one redundant owner/shape preparation pass and eliminate it or make the final consumer own the data; retain required CPU PhysX registration.
experiments.confidence: low on savings, medium on target relevance
experiments.experiment_cost: one focused source/timeline attribution pass, then a coherent lifecycle change and focused physical checks
experiments.support: Fewer duplicate allocations/scans/joins and lower unprofiled full-step time; exact import/topology/load state and accepted correction/motion quality across full suite and warm runs.
experiments.refute: Preparation is required once, CPU cost overlaps necessary GPU work, or full-step time fails to improve. A neutral architectural change needs a concrete removed dependency/follow-up.

experiments.hypothesis: Transfer only changed compatibility data and batch metadata at mandatory joins
experiments.evidence: Large idle first tick uploads about20 MB but reads back only1288 bytes; late debris transfers about42 MB H2D and43 MB D2H. These include ordinary physics and cold initialization, so attribution is required.
experiments.mechanism: Remove redundant host mirrors or whole-capacity transfers in destruction integration; publish dirty owner/chunk ranges and combine small receipts without deferring data.
scenarios: warm intact idle and warm heavy trajectory
experiments.confidence: low until destruction ownership and warm persistence established
experiments.experiment_cost: copy-site attribution plus one changed-data or receipt-batching change
experiments.support: Lower required transfer count/bytes or blocking latency and lower full-step time in matched unprofiled runs, with unchanged current-tick contacts/queries and sleep.
experiments.refute: Transfers originate in necessary PhysX state uploads, disappear naturally after cold restore, overlap other work, or savings do not reach full-step time.

experiments.hypothesis: Remove repeated stress setup or decompose necessary component work before parameter tuning
experiments.evidence: Stress dominates selected large-debris kernel time. Dense structures use a distinct persistent solver family; sparse chains and cities use component stress kernels. Low sampled DRAM rates alone do not establish the bottleneck.
experiments.mechanism: Attribute current topology/revision setup versus recurrence, then eliminate one redundant setup/reduction or rebalance independent components while preserving convergence within the tick.
experiments.confidence: low on mechanism/savings, high that stress is a material GPU cost
experiments.experiment_cost: targeted source/counter attribution, one algorithmic hypothesis, solver quality checks and full application A/B
experiments.support: Less necessary work or shorter critical stress launches with unchanged convergence/material/motion gates and verified application savings across semantic scenarios.
experiments.refute: Setup is already reused, dependency changes alter equilibrium, gains regress other structures, or GPU-only improvement fails to reduce full-step time.
